verdicts.title: Lifting to Parity Decision Trees Via Stifling
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that the deterministic decision tree complexity of a (partial) function or relation $f$ lifts to the deterministic parity decision tree (PDT) size complexity of the composed function/relation $f \circ g$ as long as the gadget $g$ satisfies a property that we call stifling. We observe that several simple gadgets of constant size, like Indexing on 3 input bits, Inner Product on 4 input bits, Majority on 3 input bits and random functions, satisfy this property. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns lifting decision-tree complexity to parity decision tree SIZE via 'stifling' gadgets, not the deterministic two-party communication complexity bound CC(f∘G^n) ≥ Q(f) via coarse-geometric pullback. It shares the lifting framework vocabulary but does not address the Roe-algebra/asymptotic-dimension route or the multiplicity-doubling argument in the conjecture.

verdicts.title: One-way communication complexity and non-adaptive decision trees
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We study the relationship between various one-way communication complexity measures of a composed function with the analogous decision tree complexity of the outer function. We consider two gadgets: the AND function on 2 inputs, and the Inner Product on a constant number of inputs. Let $IP$ denote Inner Product on $2b$ bits.

It neither establishes nor refutes a Q(f)-style two-way lower bound for f∘IND_b^n via the proposed coarse-cover route.

verdicts.title: Soft Decision Tree classifier: explainable and extendable PyTorch implementation
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We implemented a Soft Decision Tree (SDT) and a Short-term Memory Soft Decision Tree (SM-SDT) using PyTorch. The methods were extensively tested on simulated and clinical datasets. The SDT was visualized to demonstrate the potential for its explainability. SDT, SM-SDT, and XGBoost demonstrated similar area under the curve (AUC) values. These methods were better than Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Decision Tree.
